When morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people conspired against Jesus to put Him to death.
Now when it was morning, all the chief priests and those in authority took thought together with the purpose of putting Jesus to death.
到了早晨，眾祭司長和民間的長老大家商議要治死耶穌，
They bound Him, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate the governor.
And they put cords on him and took him away, and gave him up to Pilate, the ruler.
就把他捆綁，解去，交給巡撫彼拉多。
When Judas, who had betrayed Him, saw that Jesus was condemned, he was filled with remorse and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.
Then Judas, who was false to him, seeing that he was to be put to death, in his regret took back the thirty bits of silver to the chief priests and those in authority,
這時候，賣耶穌的猶大看見耶穌已經定了罪，就後悔，把那三十塊錢拿回來給祭司長和長老，說：
“I have sinned by betraying innocent blood,” he said. “What is that to us?” they replied. “You bear the responsibility.”
Saying, I have done wrong in giving into your hands an upright man. But they said, What is that to us? it is your business.
「我賣了無辜之人的血是有罪了。」他們說：「那與我們有甚麼相干？你自己承當吧！」
So Judas threw the silver into the temple and left. Then he went away and hanged himself.
And he put down the silver in the Temple and went out, and put himself to death by hanging.
猶大就把那銀錢丟在殿裡，出去吊死了。
The chief priests picked up the pieces of silver and said, “It is unlawful to put this into the treasury, since it is blood money.”
And the chief priests took the silver and said, It is not right to put it in the Temple store for it is the price of blood.
祭司長拾起銀錢來，說：「這是血價，不可放在庫裡。」
After conferring together, they used the money to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for foreigners.
And they made a decision to get with the silver the potter's field, as a place for the dead of other countries.
他們商議，就用那銀錢買了窯戶的一塊田，為要埋葬外鄉人。
That is why it has been called the Field of Blood to this day.
For this cause that field was named, The field of blood, to this day.
所以那塊田直到今日還叫做「血田」。
Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: “They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price set on Him by the people of Israel,
Then came true that which was said by Jeremiah the prophet, And they took the thirty bits of silver, the price of him who was valued by the children of Israel;
這就應了先知耶利米的話，說：「他們用那三十塊錢，就是被估定之人的價錢，是以色列人中所估定的，
and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord had commanded me.”
And they gave them for the potter's field, as I had word from the Lord.
買了窯戶的一塊田；這是照著主所吩咐我的。」
Meanwhile Jesus stood before the governor, who questioned Him: “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.
And Jesus was before the ruler, who put a question to him, Are you the King of the Jews? And Jesus said to him, You say so.
耶穌站在巡撫面前；巡撫問他說：「你是猶太人的王嗎？」耶穌說：「你說的是。」
And when He was accused by the chief priests and elders, He gave no answer.
But when the chief priests and those in authority made statements against him, he gave no answer.
他被祭司長和長老控告的時候，甚麼都不回答。
Then Pilate asked Him, “Do You not hear how many charges they are bringing against You?”
Then says Pilate to him, Do you give no attention to what their witnesses say against you?
彼拉多就對他說：「他們作見證告你這麼多的事，你沒有聽見嗎？」
But Jesus gave no answer, not even to a single charge, much to the governor’s amazement.
And he gave him no answer, not even a word: so that the ruler was greatly surprised.
耶穌仍不回答，連一句話也不說，以致巡撫甚覺希奇。
Now it was the governor’s custom at the feast to release to the crowd a prisoner of their choosing.
Now at the feast it was the way for the ruler to let free to the people one prisoner, at their selection.
巡撫有一個常例，每逢這節期，隨眾人所要的釋放一個囚犯給他們。
At that time they were holding a notorious prisoner named Barabbas.
And they had then an important prisoner, whose name was Barabbas.
當時有一個出名的囚犯叫巴拉巴。
So when the crowd had assembled, Pilate asked them, “Which one do you want me to release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
So when they came together, Pilate said to them, Whom will you have? Barabbas, or Jesus, who is named Christ?
眾人聚集的時候，彼拉多就對他們說：「你們要我釋放哪一個給你們？是巴拉巴呢？是稱為基督的耶穌呢？」
For he knew it was out of envy that they had handed Jesus over to him.
For he saw that for envy they had given him up.
巡撫原知道他們是因為嫉妒才把他解了來。
While Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him this message: “Have nothing to do with that innocent man, for I have suffered terribly in a dream today because of Him.”
And while he was on the judge's seat, his wife sent to him, saying, Have nothing to do with that upright man, for I have had much trouble this day in a dream because of him.
正坐堂的時候，他的夫人打發人來說：「這義人的事，你一點不可管，因為我今天在夢中為他受了許多的苦。」
But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus put to death.
Now the chief priests and those in authority got the people to make request for Barabbas, and for Jesus to be put to death.
祭司長和長老挑唆眾人，求釋放巴拉巴，除滅耶穌。
“Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” asked the governor. “Barabbas,” they replied.
But the ruler made answer and said to them, Which of the two is it your pleasure that I let go free? And they said, Barabbas.
巡撫對眾人說：「這兩個人，你們要我釋放哪一個給你們呢？」他們說：「巴拉巴。」
“What then should I do with Jesus who is called Christ?” Pilate asked. They all answered, “Crucify Him!”
Pilate says to them, What, then, am I to do with Jesus, who is named Christ? They all say, Let him be put to death on the cross.
彼拉多說：「這樣，那稱為基督的耶穌我怎麼辦他呢？」他們都說：「把他釘十字架！」
“Why?” asked Pilate. “What evil has He done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!”
And he said, Why, what evil has he done? But they gave loud cries, saying, To the cross with him!
巡撫說：「為甚麼呢？他做了甚麼惡事呢？」他們便極力地喊著說：「把他釘十字架！」

When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but that instead a riot was breaking out, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd. “I am innocent of this man’s blood,” he said. “You bear the responsibility.”

So when Pilate saw that he was able to do nothing, but that trouble was working up, he took water and, washing his hands before the people, said, The blood of this upright man is not on my hands: you are responsible.
彼拉多見說也無濟於事，反要生亂，就拿水在眾人面前洗手，說：「流這義人的血，罪不在我，你們承當吧。」
All the people answered, “His blood be on us and on our children!”
And all the people made answer and said, Let his blood be on us, and on our children.
眾人都回答說：「他的血歸到我們和我們的子孫身上。」
So Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified.
Then he let Barabbas go free: but after having Jesus whipped, he gave him up to be put to death on the cross.
於是彼拉多釋放巴拉巴給他們，把耶穌鞭打了，交給人釘十字架。
Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium and gathered the whole company around Him.
Then the ruler's armed men took Jesus into the open square, and got all their band together.
巡撫的兵就把耶穌帶進衙門，叫全營的兵都聚集在他那裡。
They stripped Him and put a scarlet robe on Him.
And they took off his clothing, and put on him a red robe.
他們給他脫了衣服，穿上一件朱紅色袍子，
And they twisted together a crown of thorns and set it on His head. They put a staff in His right hand and knelt down before Him to mock Him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”

And they made a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and put a rod in his right hand, and they went down on their knees before him, and made sport of him, saying, Long life to the King of the Jews.
用荊棘編做冠冕，戴在他頭上，拿一根葦子放在他右手裡，跪在他面前，戲弄他，說：「恭喜，猶太人的王啊！」
Then they spit on Him and took the staff and struck Him on the head repeatedly.
And they put shame on him, and gave him blows on the head with the rod.
又吐唾沫在他臉上，拿葦子打他的頭。
After they had mocked Him, they removed the robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him away to crucify Him.
And when they had made sport of him, they took the robe off him, and put his clothing on him, and took him away to put him on the cross.
戲弄完了，就給他脫了袍子，仍穿上他自己的衣服，帶他出去，要釘十字架。
Along the way they found a man from Cyrene, named Simon, and they forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.
And while they were coming out, they saw a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, and they made him go with them, so that he might take up his cross.
他們出來的時候，遇見一個古利奈人，名叫西門，就勉強他同去，好背著耶穌的十字架。
And when they came to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull,
And when they came to the place named Golgotha, that is to say, Dead Man's Head,
到了一個地方名叫各各他，意思就是「髑髏地」。
they offered Him wine to drink, mixed with gall; but after tasting it, He refused to drink it.
They gave him wine mixed with bitter drink: and after tasting it, he took no more.
兵丁拿苦膽調和的酒給耶穌喝。他嘗了，就不肯喝。
When they had crucified Him, they divided up His garments by casting lots.
And when they had put him on the cross, they made division of his clothing among them by the decision of chance.
他們既將他釘在十字架上，就拈鬮分他的衣服，
And sitting down, they kept watch over Him there.
And they were seated there watching him.
又坐在那裡看守他。
Above His head they posted the written charge against Him: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
And they put up over his head the statement of his crime in writing, THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
在他頭以上安一個牌子，寫著他的罪狀，說：「這是猶太人的王耶穌。」
Two robbers were crucified with Him, one on His right hand and the other on His left.
Then two thieves were put on crosses with him, one on the right and one on the left.
當時，有兩個強盜和他同釘十字架，一個在右邊，一個在左邊。
And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads
And those who went by said bitter words to him, shaking their heads and saying,
從那裡經過的人譏誚他，搖著頭，說：
and saying, “You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save Yourself! If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”
You who would give the Temple to destruction and put it up again in three days, get yourself free: if you are the Son of God, come down from the cross.
「你這拆毀聖殿、三日又建造起來的，可以救自己吧！你如果是神的兒子，就從十字架上下來吧！」
In the same way, the chief priests, scribes, and elders mocked Him, saying,
In the same way, the chief priests, making sport of him, with the scribes and those in authority, said,
祭司長和文士並長老也是這樣戲弄他，說：
“He saved others, but He cannot save Himself. He is the King of Israel! Let Him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in Him.
A saviour of others, he has no salvation for himself. If he is the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will have faith in him.
「他救了別人，不能救自己。他是以色列的王，現在可以從十字架上下來，我們就信他。
He trusts in God. Let God deliver Him now if He wants Him. For He said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”
He put his faith in God; let God be his saviour now, if he will have him; for he said, I am the Son of God.
他倚靠神，神若喜悅他，現在可以救他；因為他曾說：『我是神的兒子。』」
In the same way, even the robbers who were crucified with Him berated Him.
And the thieves who were on the crosses said evil words to him.
那和他同釘的強盜也是這樣地譏誚他。
From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.
Now from the sixth hour it was dark over all the land till the ninth hour.
從午正到申初，遍地都黑暗了。
About the ninth hour Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
And about the ninth hour Jesus gave a loud cry, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is, My God, my God, why are you turned away from me?
約在申初，耶穌大聲喊著說：「以利！以利！拉馬撒巴各大尼？」就是說：「我的神！我的神！為甚麼離棄我？」
When some of those standing there heard this, they said, “He is calling Elijah.”
And some of those who were near by, hearing it, said, This man is crying to Elijah.
站在那裡的人，有的聽見就說：「這個人呼叫以利亞呢！」
One of them quickly ran and brought a sponge. He filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and held it up for Jesus to drink.
And straight away one of them went quickly, and took a sponge, and made it full of bitter wine, and put it on a rod and gave him drink.
內中有一個人趕緊跑去，拿海絨蘸滿了醋，綁在葦子上，送給他喝。
But the others said, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him.”
And the rest said, Let him be; let us see if Elijah will come to his help.
其餘的人說：「且等著，看以利亞來救他不來。」
When Jesus had cried out again in a loud voice, He yielded up His spirit.
And Jesus gave another loud cry, and gave up his spirit.
耶穌又大聲喊叫，氣就斷了。
At that moment the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth quaked and the rocks were split.
And the curtain of the Temple was parted in two from end to end; and there was an earth-shock; and the rocks were broken;
忽然，殿裡的幔子從上到下裂為兩半，地也震動，磐石也崩裂，
The tombs broke open, and the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised.
And the resting-places of the dead came open; and the bodies of a number of sleeping saints came to life;
墳墓也開了，已睡聖徒的身體多有起來的。
After Jesus’ resurrection, when they had come out of the tombs, they entered the holy city and appeared to many people.
And coming out of their resting-places, after he had come again from the dead, they went into the holy town and were seen by a number of people.
到耶穌復活以後，他們從墳墓裡出來，進了聖城，向許多人顯現。
When the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and all that had happened, they were terrified and said, “Truly this was the Son of God.”
Now the captain and those who were with him watching Jesus, when they saw the earth-shock and the things which were done, were in great fear and said, Truly this was a son of God.
百夫長和一同看守耶穌的人看見地震並所經歷的事，就極其害怕，說：「這真是神的兒子了！」
And many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee to minister to Him.
And a number of women were there, watching from a distance, who had come with Jesus from Galilee, waiting on his needs.
有好些婦女在那裡，遠遠地觀看；她們是從加利利跟隨耶穌來服事他的。
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.
Among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary, the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
內中有抹大拉的馬利亞，又有雅各和約西的母親馬利亞，並有西庇太兩個兒子的母親。
When it was evening, there came a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph, who himself was a disciple of Jesus.
And in the evening, there came a man of wealth from Arimathaea, Joseph by name, who was a disciple of Jesus:
到了晚上，有一個財主，名叫約瑟，是亞利馬太來的，他也是耶穌的門徒。
He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus, and Pilate ordered that it be given to him.
This man went in to Pilate, and made a request for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate gave orders for it to be given to him.
這人去見彼拉多，求耶穌的身體；彼拉多就吩咐給他。
So Joseph took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
And Joseph took the body, folding it in clean linen,
約瑟取了身體，用乾淨細麻布裹好，
and placed it in his own new tomb that he had cut into the rock. Then he rolled a great stone across the entrance to the tomb and went away.
And put it in the resting-place which had been cut out of the rock for himself; and after rolling a great stone to the door of it he went away.
安放在自己的新墳墓裡，就是他鑿在磐石裡的。他又把大石頭滾到墓門口，就去了。
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were sitting there opposite the tomb.
And Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, seated by the place of the dead.
有抹大拉的馬利亞和那個馬利亞在那裡，對著墳墓坐著。
The next day, the one after Preparation Day, the chief priests and Pharisees assembled before Pilate.
Now on the day after the getting ready of the Passover, the chief priests and Pharisees came together to Pilate,
次日，就是預備日的第二天，祭司長和法利賽人聚集來見彼拉多，說：
“Sir,” they said, “we remember that while He was alive that deceiver said, ‘After three days I will rise again.’
Saying, Sir, we have in mind how that false man said, while he was still living, After three days I will come again from the dead.
「大人，我們記得那誘惑人的還活著的時候曾說：『三日後我要復活。』

So give the order that the tomb be secured until the third day. Otherwise, His disciples may come and steal Him away and tell the people He has risen from the dead. And this last deception would be worse than the first.”

Give orders, then, that the place where his body is may be made safe till the third day, for fear that his disciples come and take him away secretly and say to the people, He has come back from the dead: and the last error will be worse than the first.
因此，請吩咐人將墳墓把守妥當，直到第三日，恐怕他的門徒來，把他偷了去，就告訴百姓說：『他從死裡復活了。』這樣，那後來的迷惑比先前的更利害了！」
“You have a guard,” Pilate said. “Go, make the tomb as secure as you know how.”
Pilate said to them, You have watchmen; go and make it as safe as you are able.
彼拉多說：「你們有看守的兵，去吧！盡你們所能的把守妥當。」
So they went and secured the tomb by sealing the stone and posting the guard.
So they went, and made safe the place where his body was, putting a stamp on the stone, and the watchmen were with them.
他們就帶著看守的兵同去，封了石頭，將墳墓把守妥當。
